title: M5 contextual retrieval versus priority-only D1 selection
purpose: Deterministic retrieval-mechanism benchmark over explicitly synthetic fixture rows. It measures whether query-aware lexical ranking places the intended reference in the top three better than the existing priority-only order. It does not evaluate actual Assamese naturalness or prove semantic retrieval quality.
privacy_and_provenance: All candidates are synthetic benchmark fixtures, not runtime data, not native-verified dialect claims, and not a language corpus. Production retrieval still requires cleared source rights and two distinct native-speaker approvals.

candidates.dialect_scope: candidate regional style; review required in production
candidates.context_summary: The user says their mood is low and does not want an immediate advice checklist.
candidates.user_example: Aji mood tu bhal nai yaar. Honestly, eku koribo mon ja nai.
candidates.response_example: Acknowledge the feeling briefly and offer space before advice.
candidates.usage_notes: Be gentle; ask at most one question if it helps.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not use playful framing for serious distress.

candidates.context_summary: The user shares that they got selected for a job after trying for a long time.
candidates.user_example: I got selected for the job! Bohut din dhori try kori asilu.
candidates.response_example: Congratulate the user warmly without theatrical performance.

candidates.context_summary: The user is anxious about an upcoming exam and wants help with pressure.
candidates.user_example: Kalir exam loi bohut tension hoi ase.
candidates.response_example: Acknowledge exam pressure and ask which part worries them most.
candidates.usage_notes: Acknowledge first; keep the answer short.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not start with a long lecture.

candidates.context_summary: The user missed the previous line and asks to hear that line slowly again.
candidates.user_example: Repeat just that last line slowly, please.
candidates.response_example: Repeat only the relevant line more slowly and preserve its meaning.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not restart a long answer.

candidates.context_summary: The user requests a formal written translation about submitting an application tomorrow.
candidates.user_example: Translate into formal Assamese, not casual speech: I will submit the application tomorrow.
candidates.response_example: Use formal written Assamese and preserve the commitment and date.

candidates.dialect_scope: one specified word; not a universal dialect rule
candidates.context_summary: The user asks for a preferred pronunciation of the Assamese word meaning small, closer to horu than soru.
candidates.user_example: For Assamese সৰু meaning small, try my preferred sound closer to horu, not soru.
candidates.response_example: Try the exact word target once; do not generalize the correction to other words.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not claim a universal Upper Assam standard.

candidates.context_summary: The user says something is wrong and asks to fix it, but the target is not visible in context.
candidates.user_example: Eitu tu bhal nohoi. Fix kori diya.
candidates.response_example: Ask one short clarification about what needs fixing.

candidates.context_summary: The user heard about a current Assam job notice and asks for confirmation from an official source.
candidates.user_example: Axomot etiya ekta job notice ulai ase buli hunisu. Official notice confirm kori kobo pariba?
candidates.response_example: Check the official notice; if no reliable source confirms it, say it is unverified.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not invent a date, vacancy count, or eligibility rule.

candidates.context_summary: The user wants conventional English pronunciation preserved in a mixed Assamese-English sentence.
candidates.user_example: Say in English: I am studying the system seriously.
candidates.response_example: Keep English sounds recognisably English; do not change each English s to h.
candidates.usage_notes: Apply Assamese pronunciation rules only to intended Assamese words.
candidates.avoid_when: Do not infer pronunciation from Roman letters alone.

cases.query: user says mood is low and wants empathy without immediate advice
celebrate user got selected for job after trying for long time
user anxious about upcoming exam, acknowledge the pressure
repeat the previous line slowly and do not explain it again
formal written Assamese translation of application tomorrow, no casual slang
word-specific pronunciation correction horu rather than soru for small
ambiguous fix this request needs a short clarifying question
verify current Assam job notice with official source and uncertainty
English pronunciation control preserve the s in study system seriously inside mixed speech
